lemma lt_trichotomy (a b : α) : a < b ∨ a = b ∨ b < a :=
  Or.elim (le_total a b)
    (fun h : a ≤ b =>
      Or.elim (Decidable.lt_or_eq_of_le h) (fun h : a < b => Or.inl h) fun h : a = b =>
        Or.inr (Or.inl h))
    fun h : b ≤ a =>
    Or.elim (Decidable.lt_or_eq_of_le h) (fun h : b < a => Or.inr (Or.inr h)) fun h : b = a =>
      Or.inr (Or.inl h.symm)

/--
`flip f a b` is `f b a`. It is useful for "point-free" programming,
since it can sometimes be used to avoid introducing variables.
For example, `(·<·)` is the less-than relation,
and `flip (·<·)` is the greater-than relation.
-/
@[inline] def flip {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {φ : Sort w} (f : α → β → φ) : β → α → φ :=
  fun b a => f a b

theorem wellFounded_of_trans_of_irrefl (r : α → α → Prop) [IsTrans α r] [IsIrrefl α r] :
    WellFounded r := by
  classical
  cases nonempty_fintype α
  have (x y) (hxy : r x y) : #{z | r z x} < #{z | r z y} :=
    Finset.card_lt_card <| by
      simp only [Finset.lt_iff_ssubset.symm, lt_iff_le_not_le, Finset.le_iff_subset,

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

/--
`flip f a b` is `f b a`. It is useful for "point-free" programming,
since it can sometimes be used to avoid introducing variables.
For example, `(·<·)` is the less-than relation,
and `flip (·<·)` is the greater-than relation.
-/
@[inline] def flip {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {φ : Sort w} (f : α → β → φ) : β → α → φ :=
  fun b a => f a b
